questions.question: Build the appropriation account of Khumalo and Smit Traders from a net profit of R480 000 and prove that the whole profit is distributed.
questions.expected_answer: Net profit of R480 000 enters on the credit side of the appropriation account. The agreement is executed in order: interest on capital at 8 percent — R40 000 to Khumalo and R20 000 to Smit, R60 000 together; partners' salaries — R132 000 to Khumalo and R156 000 to Smit, R288 000 together; and a bonus of R12 000 to Smit for meeting the sales target. That appropriates R360 000, leaving R120 000, shared two to one: R80 000 to Khumalo and R40 000 to Smit. Proof: Khumalo receives R40 000 plus R132 000 plus R80 000 — R252 000; Smit receives R20 000 plus R156 000 plus R12 000 plus R40 000 — R228 000; and R252 000 plus R228 000 equals R480 000, so the account balances and the whole profit is distributed. Partners' salaries and interest on capital are appropriations of profit, never expenses, so they do not reduce net profit.

questions.question: Write up both partners' current accounts for the year, including Smit's opening debit balance, and interpret each closing balance.
questions.expected_answer: Khumalo's current account: credit side — balance brought down R9 600, interest on capital R40 000, salary R132 000, share of remaining profit R80 000, totalling R261 600; debit side — drawings R214 000; closing balance R47 600 credit, meaning the business owes Khumalo R47 600. Smit's current account opens with R6 300 on the debit side because last year she drew more than she earned. Credit side — interest on capital R20 000, salary R156 000, bonus R12 000, profit share R40 000, totalling R228 000; debit side — the opening R6 300 plus drawings of R195 500, totalling R201 800; closing balance R26 200 credit, meaning she has worked out of the debit and the business now owes her R26 200. Capital contributions never appear here — they belong in the fixed capital accounts. Together the current accounts hold R73 800 of undrawn earnings that joins capital in equity.

questions.question: Analyse these events on the accounting equation: Smit contributes R60 000 by EFT; Khumalo takes stock of R4 200 for personal use; interest on capital of R40 000 is allowed to Khumalo; interest of R22 000 is capitalised on the loan; a creditor is paid R16 500.
questions.expected_answer: The method is to write the double entry, classify each account, then read the effects. Capital contribution: debit Bank, credit Capital — assets up R60 000, equity up R60 000, liabilities nil. Stock taken: debit Drawings, credit Trading stock at cost — assets down R4 200, equity down R4 200, liabilities nil. Interest on capital allowed: debit Appropriation, credit Current account of Khumalo — both equity accounts, so total equity is unchanged; the allowance redistributes equity from the profit pool to Khumalo's claim, with no effect on assets or liabilities. Capitalised interest: debit Interest on loan, credit Loan — equity down R22 000, liabilities up R22 000, assets untouched. Paying the creditor: debit Creditors control, credit Bank — assets down R16 500, liabilities down R16 500, equity untouched, because settling a debt is not an expense. In every case the equation stays level, which is the built-in check.
